added_claim_errors: Paper temporary boarding proof at the station police window is described as free. No official source supports that, and the gmw/12306 article A cites does not say it (key trap).

Temporary ID card in the home county 'usually issued on the spot or within 3 days', repeated in the opening summary. The 3-day part is fine; 'on the spot' leans toward the key's trap that the card can be had the same day.
Photo receipt costs '20-30 yuan'. The key says the cost varies by place, so this range is unverifiable.
'Guangzhou has accepted out-of-province renewals and replacements since March 2017'. Unverifiable; the key only gives the national date of 1 July 2017.
'12306 QR code refreshes every 60 seconds'. Unverifiable.
The Liwan police link is mistyped (jczgkk) and returns 404 (I opened it). The claim it backs (40 days, 40 yuan) is correct and confirmed on the working URL.

Says you should bring one identity document (household register, residence permit, driving licence and so on). The Liwan notice I opened lists only the photo receipt for adults, so this overstates what is required.
Paper temporary boarding proof described as issued free of charge. No official source supports that, and the gmw article B cites does not say it (key trap).
'National maximum for out-of-province processing is 45 days'. Unverifiable, and it conflicts with the key's 60-day statutory limit.
EMS delivery 'in-province postage 18 yuan, paid on delivery'. Unverifiable; B's only source for it is a bendibao page, not an official one.

Household register original called 'the most critical document for a replacement', with advice to have family mail it by SF Express. The Liwan notice B itself cites lists only the photo receipt for adults. This leans toward the key's trap that a household register is required.
'New card usually takes about 30 days' in the home county. Unverifiable.
'New card arrives in mid-to-late November'. This is a guess: Guangzhou's 40-day limit from a late-October application runs to early December.
'Henan police stations usually take the photo on site'. Unverifiable.

reasons: Both answers correct the two false premises at the start and give the core facts right: 40 yuan for the replacement, a 10-yuan temporary card valid for 3 months, the 12306 electronic proof (24 hours, 6 a month), and a 60-day statutory limit with Guangzhou's 40-day promise. I confirmed the 40-day promise on the Liwan notice. Both repeat the unsupported claim that the paper station proof is free. A cites the 2017 nationwide date and gives a temporary-card section sourced to the Baiyun notice, which I opened and which supports the 5-working-day wait and the province list. B adds the unverifiable 45-day national maximum and the 18-yuan EMS fee, and overstates the household register as the most critical document, sending the user to have it mailed when B's own source does not require it. B does add useful points (hotels will not accept the boarding proof, buy the ticket now), but A's mistyped link and its 'on the spot' wording for the home-county temporary card are smaller problems than B's additions, so A wins slightly.
